newsitem.title: USA: DuPont to close Martinsville nylon plant.
newsitem.headline: DuPont to close Martinsville nylon plant.

text.p: DuPont Co. said Monday it will stop producing nylon at its Martinsville, Va., plant by mid-1998, resulting in the loss of about 600 full-time jobs.
The facility, built in 1941, was the world's second nylon plant and is a supplier to the apparel industry.
Dupont said the age of the facility and its small production capacity put it at a disadvantage to most other DuPont nylon manufacturing facilities in North America.
The company said no significant impact on plant staffing is expected before mid-1997, and that a schedule to phase out operations has not been finalised.

DuPont said it will continue to own the plant site. DuPont Precision Concepts, a supplier of precision machined parts, will maintain operations there, employing about 50 people. In addition, there will be a small site support group.
DuPont's stock fell 75 cents to $82.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
